references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the angel whom God sends ahead of the people to guard them on their journey and lead them to the place he has prepared is mentioned.
God repeats the promise to send an angel ahead of the Israelites and drive out the same nations: the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
At the burning bush, God promises to lead the Israelites out of Egypt and into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Moses repeats the list of the seven nations that the Lord will drive out ahead of the Israelites when they enter the promised land.
Joshua assures the people that the living God will drive out the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.
Joshua reminds the people how God drove out the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites before them.
The Lord tells Moses that his angel will go ahead of him and lead the people to the promised land.
The Israelites recall that God sent an angel and led them out of Egypt, which connects to the promise of the angel's guidance.
In the covenant with Abraham, several of the same nations are mentioned as those who will lose their land to Abraham's descendants.
The Lord himself will go ahead of the people and destroy the nations so that the Israelites can take possession of the land.
A theological parallel where God's direct intervention confirms the promise to drive out the nations, even though the angel is not explicitly mentioned.
